rv.q: The script was incredibly witty and the performances so delightfully comical in their individual portrayals that you couldn't help but become emotionally invested in the outcome of each.
Lord love Baltimore’s Hippodrome Theatre for being able to host this outstanding piece of show biz.
This powerhouse of a jukebox musical has made it to the stage at Clowes Memorial Hall in Indianapolis, and audiences are electrified by this production.
The national tour of & Juliet at Walton Arts Center is an absolute blast of confetti-covered joy, and Fayetteville audiences are eating up every second of it.
More often, & JULIET finds a surprisingly clever reason for them to be there.
& Juliet is an escapist, confetti-filled romp perfect for fans of Six, and Hamilton, and 90s and 2000s pop music.
It is an undeniably entertaining concept.
& Juliet presents a fresh take on a familiar story and offers a distinctly modern perspective on one of literature's most famous heroines.

Even though I had fun watching such a talented cast, I left wishing the show had stayed focused on its original story and emotional moments instead of constantly trying to outdo and overcomplicate itself.
The musical embraces contemporary ideas about identity, love and belonging in ways that feel expansive rather than performative.
Energetic, empowering, and impossibly fun, this is the kind of show that reminds you why live theater still matters.
Ultimately, whether you're a seasoned musical-theatergoer or have never seen one before, "& Juliet" provides an electric, wild ride.
The musical, at Playhouse Square through March 23, is an exhilarating production and a hell of a good time.
It’s hard to imagine anyone resisting the infectious fun of this show.
I greatly enjoyed this show and I highly recommend that anyone see it, particularly those who would recognize the music because that just adds extra fun to the experience!
The overwhelming appeal of & Juliet as an escapist, music-filled delight is undeniable.

Creators of the “& Juliet” Broadway musical took about 30 of Martin’s top tracks for a 1990s-2000s nostalgia trip that helps tell an infectiously entertaining “what if…?” story set in Shakespeare’s time with modern sensibilities.
The musical leans into being a splashy, light-hearted, unapologetic piece of toe-tapping escapism–and damn, is it successful.
& Juliet delivered a high level of exuberant energy that mixed both sentiment and satire.
"& Juliet" provides a zesty new twist on what history has labeled the greatest love story ever told.
Whether you like Shakespeare or not, “& Juliet” is an upbeat celebration of empowerment we all can learn from.
On its second Chicago engagement, & Juliet remains a glittering, joyous confection of a jukebox musical.
It didn’t detract from the absolute pleasure of getting there.
& Juliet is a giant feel-good party from beginning to end.
Webb slays, summoning determination and passion on “Roar,” the musical’s showstopping 11 o’clock number.
There's never been a version even remotely like the hilariously irreverent "& Juliet," which had Broadway shrieking in laughter and sold out a ton of dates on tour.
With nostalgia from pop songs like “Oops!… I Again,” “Since U Been Gone” and “I That Way” coupled with a hilarious campy script, it’s no wonder the show has broken attendance records.
& Juliet empowers by showing us that life is made of choices.
The ingeniously clever script sets up every song so each is the exact and perfect answer to the plot quandary at hand.
All that’s needed to have a great time with “& Juliet” is a fondness for the music you may have grown up with.
That said, it feels like it is trying to do much, skimming over the surface of the issues which are resolved too easily.

“& Juliet” echoes Baz Luhrmann, the director behind the Leonardo DiCaprio and Claire Danes-led “Romeo + Juliet,” in its frenetic pacing, penchant for montages and excess of design. With a book by David West Read, who wrote and executive produced “Schitt’s Creek,” the musical is frequently laugh-out-loud funny.
Interestingly, & Juliet proves that jukebox musicals do not have to be confined to the basement level of the high-rise of theatrical entertainment.
Perhaps inevitably, “& Juliet” can feel like an overstuffed grab bag of rom-com and pop music formulas.
Across Canada production of & Juliet boasts a talented ensemble led by Fabiola Caraballo Quijada in the title role.
Is there such a thing as Too Much Fun?
The show is fast-paced and flashy.

The manufactured bliss-point appeal of the show started to wear off in the second act, after the laugh-out-loud novelty of hearing familiar pop songs reorchestrated into a musical theater setting faded.
All in all, I will say & Juliet is a really fun, entertaining show.

cn.t: Critics celebrate this jukebox musical as a joyful, high-energy spectacle that cleverly reimagines Shakespeare with Max Martin's pop hits.
